summary: Owned units s0178–s0199 contain no birth, death, or age statements; Wang Xizhi's fifty-nine-sui death and Xie Wan's later defeat sit outside this slice. The Danyang gathering cluster (Liu Tan, Xu Xun, Wang Xizhi) is explicitly undated in the chapter and was given AD 347–349 from Liu Tan's external tenure. That reconstruction is right in outline—appointment in Yonghe 3/12, death in office before Chu Pou's Yonghe 5/12 death—but the lower Western bound is wrong: Yonghe 3/12 falls in January 348, so onOrAfter 347 allows a year before the documented start. The chapter's placement of 時劉惔為丹陽尹 after the 355 tomb-vow is a narrative order, not Liu Tan's own later activity; dating the gathering by his Danyang tenure rather than by the vow is correct. Wang's leisure, the first Xie Wan letter, the eastern return, and Xie An's planned tour are supported on or after the Yonghe 11/3 oath (AD 355) and before Xie Wan's Shengping 2/8 Yuzhou appointment (AD 358). The Yuzhou command in 358 and the 359 defeat hint match the Mu Di annals. Chao Fu, Xu You, Ji, and Qi remain legendary exempla. Lu Jia, Ban Si, and Yang Wangsun are undated in their own lives and correctly kept off active hints; their citation in the leisure letter is retrospective reception dated to that letter.

itemChecks.event: Liu Tan is attested as Danyang governor during Xu Xun's overnight stay.
itemChecks.reason: The chapter only says 時劉惔為丹陽尹, with no reign year. Jiankang Shilu, under Jin Mu Di Yonghe 3, records the Danyang appointment in winter, twelfth month. That lunar month begins 348-01-17 on the verified Yonghe conversion table (Julian before 1582, the Academia Sinica default; proleptic Gregorian is one day earlier and stays AD 348). onOrAfter AD 347 therefore treats the conventional Yonghe-3 year-label as if every month were Gregorian 347 and allows an impossible year before the documented tenure. The end bound onOrBefore AD 349 is the right year-precision terminus: Jin Shu says Liu died in that office at thirty-six sui, and Sun Chuo spoke of him as already dead while Chu Pou still lived; Chu Pou died on Yonghe 5/12/己酉. Revise the lower bound to onOrAfter AD 348; do not invent an exact year.

The 355–358 interval is therefore a window of uncertainty for the letter snapshot, not a demonstrated continuous 吏部郎 tenure through 358. It does not invent a second endpoint.

The cautionary letter is narrated immediately after that appointment and before the later defeat; year 358 dates the command, not a guessed letter-only year.

personChecks.reason: Owned rows all date Liu Tan's Danyang governorship and the Xu Xun lodging to AD 347–349. The office is explicit in s0179; the Western start is not. Yonghe 3/12 converts to January 348, so 347 is not a possible year of this office. Jin Shu 075 records death in office at thirty-six sui with no year; Chu Pou, who discussed him as already dead, died Yonghe 5/12, so onOrBefore 349 remains a justified end bound. This chapter slice has no birth. Owner of the dated events is Liu Tan himself, not a descendant or later commemorator.

Xu Xun's only dated event here is lodging with Liu Tan while Tan was Danyang governor. That event cannot precede the Yonghe 3/12 appointment (January 348) and cannot postdate Liu Tan's death-in-office terminus of 349. The 347 start is therefore incoherent. No birth or death is stated for Xu Xun in the owned units.

Wang Xizhi has two personal chronologies in this slice: presence at the Danyang gathering (s0182) and post-oath leisure with the Xie Wan letters and eastern return (s0184, s0188). Dating the gathering by Liu Tan's Danyang tenure, not by the chapter's later placement after 朝廷以其誓苦，亦不復征之, is the right reading of whose event is dated: Liu Tan was already dead by 349, so 羲之在坐 cannot be post-355 living activity with him. The gathering's 347 lower bound is still the wrong conversion. Leisure on or after 355 is supported by the Yonghe 11/3 oath and must stay open; context claim-543 keeps the fifty-nine-sui death undated and must not be turned into an activity end. No birth is given.
Chao Fu appears only in the hypothetical 令巢許遇稷契. Legendary antiquity is coherent; there is no Western life date to contradict and no omitted birth or death in these units.
Xu You is the other hermit in the same hypothetical pair. No living Eastern Jin chronology is claimed.
Ji is invoked as an ancient minister in the same sentence. Qualitative antiquity is complete for this mention.
Qi is invoked with Ji as an ancient minister. Qualitative antiquity is complete for this mention.

Xie Wan's owned events form a sequence: first letter while 吏部郎 after Wang's 355 leisure (s0184), then 豫州都督 in 358 (s0195), then the 359 defeat retained as a context item and hint. Jin Shu Mu Di Shengping 2/8 and 3/10 confirm the last two years. The 355–358 gentleman interval is a letter window, and by Shengping 2/8 he was already 吳興太守, so it must not be read as tenure through 358. No birth or death is stated in the owned units; the biography's later age at death is outside this job.

Xie An's only owned event is the planned eastern tour in the leisure letter (s0192). That plan is dated by the letter window 355–358. Context p058's on-or-after-355 hint is consistent and is not used here as an extra life date. No birth or death appears in the owned units.

Lu Jia has an undated own-life attestation and a retrospective citation dated to Wang's letter. Empty hints correctly refuse to treat the reception as living activity. No birth or death is in this chapter slice.

Jiankang Shilu dates the appointment to Yonghe 3, winter, twelfth month, which converts to January 348. onOrAfter 347 therefore allows a year before the documented start.
findings.action: Replace onOrAfter AD 347 with onOrAfter AD 348 on claim-457, claim-458, claim-459, claim-482, claim-483 and the matching hints for p059, p060, and the first p061 hint.
